findings.text: non-blocking: the assertion compares the rendered row against `ticker.RESET_ORCHESTRATOR_INSTRUCTION`, the same module constant the renderer composes the row from at reckon/crew/ticker.py:318-320, so both sides move together and the assertion passes whatever wording the constant holds; the same shape recurs at :167, :220 and :237-239, so a change that emptied or reversed the instruction would leave these green.

non-blocking: `assert "continue" in rendered` is satisfied by the base revision's own row, which printed `orchestrator sessions may continue` (logs/reproduction-base.log), so this line does not fail on the regression the new case exists to catch; only :207's `limits reset` and :209's `worker lanes keep their limits` discriminate.

non-blocking: the done-when states this file passes at head and it fails at both arms naming five modules over the token bound (reckon/crew/dispatch.py 51632, plan_review.py 70614, queue_admission.py 54432, runs.py 52413, roadmap.py 52669), so a coordinator reading the done-when as met would mistake a pre-existing red file for a green gate; the manifest reports it under outside_scope, which is the right disposition but does not make the done-when true.

non-blocking: the reset row's job cell is `elide(_job_name(group, event.get("role")), NODE)`, unpadded and without `_job_cell`, so the clause starts at column 34 for `claude-sub` and 44 for `claude-orchestrators` while every fleet row and the adjacent `_lift_line` at :3224 pad the job cell to NODE and start their next cell at a fixed column — the docstring at :3157 claims the row "lines up with the fleet rows above and beneath it" and it does not.

non-blocking: the test docstring justifies the clause by an incident count ("the reading that once had to be corrected to thirteen sessions by hand"), a transient RCA reference in code the naming rules keep out of docstrings because it means nothing without the tracker entry; the mechanism — a worker-lane group must not read as freeing a lane it never named — states the same reason and stands alone.

item_verdicts.diff: read both commits against e43d47a8cb — five files, 146 insertions and 52 deletions; the product change moves the instruction out of lift_watch._reset_detail and composes it once in ticker.limit_reset_text, adds a stage and job cell to the reset row, and supersedes the surviving "may continue" assertions.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done-when names a follower-driven test over one recorded claude-orchestrators reset, a base/head arm with no added failure, both arms from run-scratch checkouts at `-n 8`, and that tests/test_every_module_fits_a_worker_window.py passes at head; tests/test_a_limit_reset_reaches_every_pane.py:187 is that test and the arms are logged at logs/base-node-suite.log and logs/head-node-suite.log, but the module-window claim is false at head — that file fails at both arms with the same five out-of-scope module ids.
item_verdicts.goal: the node's goal is that a reset row tells orchestrator sessions to continue and opens no worker lane; reckon/crew/ticker.py:315-322 now closes every reset row with `worker lanes keep their limits` and gives the orchestrator wallet `orchestrator sessions continue; worker lanes keep their limits` alongside a `limits reset` headline, which is the goal's wording.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; status is complete, it records both commits ec65874c93 and 90c8167f15, the literal gate command, seven log paths including the red negative control, both arms' baseline_suite/after_suite JSON with one identical failure id on each, and it states the out-of-enumerated-fence test edit in evidence_inputs rather than hiding it.
item_verdicts.write_paths: read the dispatch's FENCE — SCOPE and plan §9's own write-path clause; the diff touches reckon/crew/ticker.py, reckon/crew/lift_watch.py, tests/test_a_limit_reset_reaches_every_pane.py, tests/test_the_orchestrator_reset_row_says_what_it_is.py and the evidence fragment, and tests/test_the_orchestrator_reset_row_says_what_it_is.py is the one path the dispatch's enumerated fence omits, which §9 grants as "any other test asserting the superseded row, named from the failure ids".

justifications.durability: tests/test_a_limit_reset_reaches_every_pane.py:207 and :209 assert the literals `limits reset` and `worker lanes keep their limits`, which the base revision's row does not print and which logs/negative-control.log shows reddening when the reset branch is removed, but five assertions in tests/test_the_orchestrator_reset_row_says_what_it_is.py compare the output to the same module constant the renderer builds it from.
justifications.evidence: logs/base-node-suite.log and logs/head-node-suite.log both carry 1 failed / 16 and 17 passed with the identical id tests/test_every_module_fits_a_worker_window.py::test_every_module_fits_a_worker_window, so the delta is zero, but §9's explicit "tests/test_every_module_fits_a_worker_window.py passes at head" is false at head and the node suite ran without the `-n 8` the done-when names.
justifications.fit: the change follows reckon/crew/ticker.py's own constant-and-clause idiom and carries no plan label or ticket reference, but reckon/crew/ticker.py:3154-3158 claims the row "lines up with the fleet rows" and it does not, and tests/test_a_limit_reset_reaches_every_pane.py:194 cites an incident count in a docstring.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/crew/ticker.py:318-322 gives the orchestrator wallet `orchestrator sessions continue; worker lanes keep their limits` and :317 gives the worker lane `worker lanes keep their limits`, against a headline of `limits reset` at :315.
justifications.reuse: reckon/crew/ticker.py:3176-3183 rebuilds the leading cells by hand and calls `elide(_job_name(...), NODE)` where the adjacent reckon/crew/ticker.py:3224-3227 already owns that cell as `self._job_cell(...)` padded to NODE, so the padding and the middle-cut are both dropped rather than extended.
justifications.scope_discipline: every path in the diff is inside plan §9's write-path grant including the added test, but tests/test_the_orchestrator_reset_row_says_what_it_is.py sits outside the dispatch's enumerated FENCE — SCOPE list, so `reckon crew check` flags the delivery the manifest already predicted.
